correctness.rationale: Every excited vertex-time event has refractory exclusion of two later times. Along each undirected edge consecutive-time transmissions are a matching between endpoint event sets. At least q transmissions enter every post-initial excitation, while all edge capacities sum via integer layer cake to at most rho(G)N_T. Thus (q-rho)N_T<=qm for all horizons, proving finite extinction count and timing. Exhaustive exact-rational verifier checks 11,259 labelled configurations and the boundary four-cycle for q=1,2,3; these experiments are corroboration, not the proof.

originality.rationale: Actual published-finding corpus semantic queries, accessible earlier claims and relevant full primary texts did not identify a theorem bounding *all* excitation events by maximum induced-edge density for the refractory threshold-q map. The closest finite-graph full text uses threshold one, while infinite-tree work concerns stochastic initialization. The new all-graph event-matching inequality genuinely generalizes isolated extinction instances without being implied by their exact graph-specific cutoffs; an unindexed equivalent remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed historical result could independently establish a similar density criterion.
Author-uploaded 1993 archival full text was more readable than arXiv PDF in the available retrieval; no claim of exhaustive literature coverage.

value.rationale: Gives an arbitrary-graph, all-initial and all-threshold structural obstruction to indefinite excitation using the classical densest-induced-subgraph invariant, plus a finite total-activation budget. It covers unbounded-degree wheel hubs and the entire low-maximum-degree class, and proves sharpness of the strict threshold through persistent complete bipartite examples. It is not an isolated finite census or a substitution in a prior graph-specific cutoff.
